# Feature #139 — Android TXT/MD auto-generated Contents (TOC)

Gate-5b acceptance pass. This is the **second** run of `TxtTocAcceptanceTest`: the first (2026-08-04,
WI-8) failed §5 gate 1 at 8,300–11,449 ms against a 1,500 ms budget and correctly blocked `VERIFIED`.
Feature **#172** fixed the cause; the suite is **unmodified** between the two runs.

## The user-visible path (rule 47 Gate 5 — production reachability)

**app launch → `MainActivity` (the manifest LAUNCHER activity) → Library grid → tap the book's title
tile → `TxtReaderActivity` → bottom-chrome "Contents" control → tap a chapter row → the reader
navigates and the tapped chapter becomes the highlighted row.**

No `TxtReaderActivity.intent()`, no debug launcher, no composable invoked directly. The opened reader
is additionally asserted to carry the expected fingerprint in the production intent extra.

**Static reachability**: every file on that path is in `android/app/src/main` — `MainActivity`,
`LibraryScreen`, `TxtReaderActivity`, `ReaderChromeScaffold`, `TocBookmarksSheet`,
`TocContentsSheetContent`, `TxtMdTocProvider`. `android/app/src/debug` contains only a manifest, a
`res/` tree, `BackupDebugActivity.kt` and `PreviewBackupService.kt` — none on this path.

**On the "release-configured build" clause**: no instrumentable release variant exists —
`android/app/build.gradle.kts` declares no `buildTypes` block, so `release` is unsigned (established
during feature #155's Gate 2). Verified on the debug build, which shares `src/main` with release,
plus the static proof above. This is the static-release + dynamic-debug split this project settled on.

## Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Observed | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Contents appears for a TXT book with headings | Real 14 MB CJK book → control shown, sheet lists one row per chapter | **pass** |
| 2 | Contents stays hidden for a TXT book without headings | Headings-free asset → control hidden, `chrome-notes` still present. Asserted **only after the scan completes**, so a stuck gate cannot pass it | **pass** |
| 3 | Chapter count + titles exact on the real book | `entries=1859`, first `第一章　太阳消失`, last `第一千八百六十章 左旋封锁` | **pass** |
| 4 | Every entry anchored against the real decoded bytes | `all_anchored=true` over 7,029,609 chars | **pass** |
| 5 | Tapping a row navigates — **scroll** mode | `jumped_row=3 landed_chunk=232` | **pass** |
| 6 | Tapping a row navigates — **paged** mode | Lands the pager on the page containing the chapter's offset, re-evaluated against #138's possibly-partial windowed index | **pass** |
| 7 | MD file produces nested entries with depth indentation | `docs/architecture.md` (128,381 B, sha256 `6bc996d5…fefeb6`) → **37 entries**, depths `[0,1,2,3]`; depth-2 measurably indented past depth-1 | **pass** |
| 8 | Current-chapter highlight follows reading position | `txtTocIndexFor` O(log n), verified by WI-5's differential oracle | **pass** |
| 9 | Scan within the stated 1,500 ms budget (§5 gate 1) | **74 ms** quiet, **71 ms** contended | **pass** |
| 10 | Open-to-first-page does not regress (§5 gate 2, BLOCKING PRIMARY) | quiet **71 ms**, concurrent **5 ms**, target 2,000 ms | **pass** |
| 11 | Empty-TOC case renders no empty sheet | Control hidden rather than an empty sheet — the scaffold derives visibility from emptiness | **pass** |
| 12 | Large TOC does not ANR | 2,000-entry sheet opens lazily at the current chapter; every entry reachable (WI-6) | **pass** |

**6 acceptance tests, 0 failures.** Supporting suites at this commit: 174 JVM tests across the five

## Observations

**The capability delivered**: before #139, TXT and MD books had **no chapter navigation at all** —
`TxtReaderActivity` passed `tocEntries = emptyList()` unconditionally and `ReaderChromeScaffold`'s
empty-list rule hid the Contents control on every such book. A 254,109-line CJK novel was
unnavigable. It now opens a Contents sheet with 1,859 chapters in 74 ms.

**This feature was blocked for a day, correctly.** WI-8's first acceptance run failed on the real
book and the lane reported `blocked` rather than loosening the assertion. That failure was worth more
than a pass would have been: it exposed that the plan's §5 decision against persistence rested on a
**desktop-JVM** measurement (46–102 ms) that was ~100× wrong on-device. Eight WIs had already merged
on top of that assumption, and every earlier gate passed because they used small generated fixtures.
Only the real book could show it.

**The fix was not what anyone predicted.** The orchestrator proposed a line-prefix pre-filter; the
plan's own fallback was Room persistence. Measurement (#172 WI-1) killed both: the cost was
`Matcher` construction being length-proportional on API 35, and the remedy was ~10 lines reusing one
`Matcher` driven by no-arg `find()`. Layer-2 line-start enumeration's *floor* (75–89 ms) is worse
than what layer 1 achieves (61 ms).

**Cross-WI facts that survived into the shipped behaviour**: TXT titles can legitimately contain an
embedded newline (a rule may match across a line terminator), MD titles never can — so the Contents
row collapses whitespace at presentation. And a TOC row's `canonicalLocator` is built by *calling*
`txtBookmarkLocator`, so a chapter row and a #135 bookmark at one source offset are the same
canonical position by construction.

**Brittle for next time**: fixtures are wiped by every connected run; measurements live only in
logcat; and the 2.5 GB emulator's lowmemorykiller truncated runs during the pre-fix era (it has not
recurred since the memory regression closed with the latency).
